title: Primary keys
summary: A PK uniquely identifies each row — the target of every foreign key.

exercise.solution:
from sqlalchemy import String, Integer, Numeric, Boolean, ForeignKey, UniqueConstraint, create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, mapped_column, relationship


class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass

class LabL03Country(Base):
    __tablename__ = "lab_l03_countries"
    code: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(2), primary_key=True)
    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(80))


class LabL03City(Base):
    __tablename__ = "lab_l03_cities"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(80))

engine = create_engine(DATABASE_URL)
Base.metadata.create_all(engine)

from sqlalchemy import String, Integer, Numeric, Boolean, ForeignKey, UniqueConstraint, create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, mapped_column, relationship


class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass

class LabL03Country(Base):
    __tablename__ = "lab_l03_countries"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    code: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(2), unique=True)
    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(80))


class LabL03City(Base):
    __tablename__ = "lab_l03_cities"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(80))

engine = create_engine(DATABASE_URL)
Base.metadata.create_all(engine)

body:
A PK uniquely identifies each row — the target of every foreign key.

Why it matters: Foreign keys point at primary (or unique) keys. Without a stable PK, you cannot express 1:N, 1:1, or M:N safely, and ON DELETE behavior becomes undefined.

SQL ↔ ORM: SQLAlchemy primary_key=True ↔ Prisma @id ↔ SQL PRIMARY KEY.
why: Foreign keys point at primary (or unique) keys. Without a stable PK, you cannot express 1:N, 1:1, or M:N safely, and ON DELETE behavior becomes undefined.
objectives: Mark a surrogate integer id as PRIMARY KEY.
Prefer stable surrogate keys in labs; add UNIQUE for natural keys separately.
pitfalls: Forgetting @id / primary_key=True — table exists but relationships cannot attach.
Composite PKs too early — fine in production, noisy while learning basics.
mappingNotes: SQLAlchemy primary_key=True ↔ Prisma @id ↔ SQL PRIMARY KEY.
teachAlong: Cause: row needs a durable identity.
